history.summary: One of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites (with Badrinath, Dwarka and Rameswaram). The present temple was built in the 12th century CE by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva of the Eastern Ganga dynasty in Kalinga architectural style, with a 65-metre shikhara crowned by the Neelachakra. The deities Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are made of sacred neem wood and are ritually renewed in the Nabakalebara ceremony every 12 to 19 years. The temple's mythology traces back to the Nilamadhava legend of Kantilo (see seq 1990). Only Hindus are permitted inside the sanctum; the Mahaprasad kitchen is among the world's largest.

name: Jagannath Temple
town_description: Puri is a major coastal city in Odisha on the Bay of Bengal, one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage destinations and home to the Shree Jagannath Temple. It is also known for its beaches, the annual Rath Yatra that draws millions, and the nearby Konark Sun Temple (about 35 km).

travel.airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar, about 60 km
travel.road: Puri bus stand about 1.9 km; well-connected by road from Bhubaneswar (~60 km) and Konark (~35 km)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Rath Yatra (June-July) is the grandest spectacle but extremely crowded
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opens about 5:00-5:30 AM; sources conflict on closing (9:00 PM vs 11:00 PM) (verify)
